subject: POC capacity planning — reserved GPUs & autoscaling (Acme AI)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-25T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — capacity planning notes

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion. Per request, summary of proposed POC plan and capacity requirements so we can lock timelines and get the SOW out. High level:

- POC objective / success criteria: verify integration latency and throughput on your production-like prompts and confirm cost per 1M tokens under the targeted workload; specific success metrics: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for single-turn requests at 1k qps, end-to-end throughput to sustain 3 concurrent streams of document-search+generate flow, and model-quality parity (sample-based) within 5% of your current baseline.

- Evaluation plan & ownership:
  * Test dataset & prompts: Acme to share 1000-sample evaluation set (Jordan) by 2026-03-29.
  * Validation harness: Redwood will run a 48-hour soak test using your dataset, capture latency/throughput/quality (Vivek).
  * Quality sign-off: Priya and Rahul will review samples and provide pass/fail per category.

- POC timeline:
  * SOW + infra config sign-off: target 2026-03-30
  * Provisioning + onboarding call: 2026-04-01
  * Soak + perf run: 2026-04-02 — 2026-04-03
  * Review & decision: 2026-04-06

- Capacity recommendation (initial reserved + autoscale):
  * Reserved: 2 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs dedicated for your POC (predictable throughput for correctness testing).
  * Autoscale/burst: additional burst capacity up to 6 GPUs allowed for load peaks during soak; autoscale policy will spin up to 4 additional GPUs when queue latency > 100ms for > 30s.
  * Expected steady-state throughput on reserved capacity: ~1200 tokens/sec for the common prompt profiles you shared. With autoscale to 6 GPUs peak throughput ~3600 tokens/sec.

- Cost and limits:
  * Reserved portion billed per week during POC. Bursts billed at usage rate. Estimated 7-day POC cost provided in attached SOW.

Attachments: acme-poc-capacity-sow.pdf, redwood-poc-configuration.xlsx

Next steps (action items):
1) Jordan: share evaluation dataset + example traffic profile by 2026-03-29.
2) Redwood (Vivek/Marissa): send final SOW and infra config for sign-off by 2026-03-30.
3) Priya/Rahul: confirm success criteria and any additional telemetry needs (traces, full request logs) by 2026-03-30.

If that matches your expectations I'll route the SOW for signature today.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and aligned. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset: we'll share the 1000-sample eval set tomorrow (2026-03-27). It includes 3 traffic profiles (low latency single-turn, multi-turn customer-support, and long-document summarization).
2) Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for the single-turn profile is our primary gating metric. For long-document summarization we expect higher latency but need linear scaling characteristics documented.
3) Burst expectations: during our internal load tests we sometimes spike to 5x normal qps for short windows (~2-3 minutes). Will the autoscale policy handle that without rejecting requests?

Also, quick ask — do you have an example dashboard we can preview (latency by model/route, token cost breakdown) so our infra team can confirm telemetry works with our compliance needs?

Jordan

Subject: Re: POC kickoff — capacity planning notes

Jordan — quick answers below and a short operational plan. Adding Dev for infra config details.

- Autoscale behavior: yes, the autoscaler will add capacity up to the configured burst cap (we proposed 6 GPUs). It reacts to queue length and CPU/GPU utilization; policy will be: scale out when request queue latency > 100ms for 30s, scale in after metrics stable for 120s. No requests are dropped — they queue; we can tune a soft concurrency limit to prioritize latency-sensitive routes.

- Short spikes (2-3 minutes, 5x): this is expected to be handled by autoscale within ~60-90s depending on model cold-start; to reduce cold-start penalty we recommend enabling warm pool (we'll keep 1 warm replica per additional GPU) which increases minimal burst cost but reduces spin-up to ~20-30s.

- Dashboard/access: attaching a sample Deck and a link to the Redwood Console view (token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latency by route). We'll grant your infra team read-only access for the POC.

Operational plan summary:
1) Redwood to provision reserved 2x A100-equivalent GPUs for the POC and configure autoscale to 6 GPUs.
2) Enable warm pool for burst GPUs (1 warm replica each) if Acme approves.
3) Redwood to run 48-hr soak and provide console link to results.

Dev — can you drop the exact instance types and the S3 path we'll use for logs into the shared Drive file?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
